angles.drive: You treat a promise as a fixed point. You trust being counted on more than being let off, and you carry plans you no longer want sooner than drop them. When you make fewer promises, each one you keep costs you less.

You play fair by reflex rather than by decision. You want to be judged by the same measure you judge by, and you give up every advantage only you noticed. Stay fair, since the advantage you give up usually lands with someone who thanks you.

Setting the standard is how you make a place feel steady. You trust a rule you wrote more than one you were handed, and you write one wherever none exists. If you meet the standard first, set it wherever you please.

Following the rule is where you feel surest. You would rather stand within a rule than in the open on your own call, and you follow it past its use. Remind yourself that you pay for every rule kept too long in choices never made.

Waiting for permission is your first move, whatever the move is. You would sooner have a yes from above than your own, and you hold a question until someone else answers it. You often wait on people who are themselves waiting for you.

You change late and on your own terms. You would rather keep a way that works than try one that works better, since trying is where things get lost. You protect what you have and never find out what the change would have brought.

Reliability is your signature act, performed so long it stopped being a performance. You are where you said, when you said, doing what you agreed. Whole systems, families, and rosters get planned around the fact of you holding, and you simply keep holding.

Fairness runs your decisions even when favoritism would be cheaper. The rules apply to your favorite and your rival at the same rate, and to you first of all. People may dislike your ruling. They have stopped questioning how you reached it.

Heavy things migrate to you because you keep accepting them, and structures form on top. The team’s hardest account, the family’s paperwork, the club’s finances: whatever must not fail gets filed under your name. You carry it evenly and rarely mention the tonnage.

Your pace has one setting, geological, and urgency does not shift it. The decision will be right and it will be late, in that order. Opportunities with expiry dates keep expiring in your in-tray while the due diligence achieves its usual thoroughness.

The rule outranks the situation for you, even when the situation is standing right there. Exceptions feel like structural damage, so the form gets filled, the channel gets followed, the spirit occasionally suffocates inside the letter. Order is kept. What order was for gets misplaced.

Once your position sets, it sets. New evidence arrives and finds the concrete already cured. You call it consistency, and it often is, and sometimes it is just the memory of a decision outliving every reason that made it.
